name: Casual Roll (AIFA)
mechanics: Two folds, cuff-width each, left slightly undone.
avoid: Client-facing days — unravels easily, reads unpolished.

name: Italian Roll
mechanics: Cuff flipped high inside-out, folded down once to peek 2-3cm.

name: Master Roll
mechanics: Two precise folds, cuff fully covered but its top edge.
effect: Most polished roll, striking with a contrast cuff lining.

name: Garter Roll
mechanics: Elastic garter with metal clasps locks the roll in place.

name: High Roll (Bicep)
mechanics: Roll continues to the lower bicep, elbow bone left covered.

name: No Break
mechanics: Hem grazes the shoe top, no fold.

name: Quarter Break
mechanics: Small, subtle crease at the front of the shoe.

name: Half Break
mechanics: One clear crease, hem ~1/2" past the shoe top.
effect: The common default, not the tallest option.
avoid: One notch more than ideal at 172cm.

name: Full Break
mechanics: Fold runs fully around the leg, cloth rests on the shoe.
avoid: Avoid — the single most height-shortening trouser choice.

name: Full Tuck
mechanics: Entire shirt hem into the waistband, all the way around.
effect: Most formal, raises the visual waistline.

name: French Tuck
mechanics: Only front-centre tucks; sides/back stay loose.
avoid: Not polished enough for client-facing days.

name: Military Tuck
mechanics: Full tuck, then smooth and pinch fabric back at each hip bone.
use: Fitted look under a blazer for important days.

name: Untucked (correct hem)
mechanics: Straight-cut hem, ends near the fly.
effect: Correctly casual only with the right hem shape.
avoid: Never leave a curved dress-shirt hem untucked.

name: Spread Collar
mechanics: Wide point angle.
effect: Flatters narrow/oval faces, wider tie knots.

name: Semi-Spread Collar
mechanics: Moderate point angle.
effect: Safe default, works on most face shapes.

name: Button-Down Collar
mechanics: Narrow spread, points button down.
effect: Suits rounder faces — your daily register.

name: Band Collar
mechanics: No fold-over collar, narrow standing band.

name: Column of Colour
mechanics: One tonal family top-to-shoe, texture varies within it.

name: Belt & Shoe Leather
mechanics: Same leather family, not an exact match.
use: Always, except when the shoe is deliberately a statement colour.
avoid: Never mix black and brown leather.

name: Socks Match Trousers
mechanics: Dress socks match trousers, not shoes.
avoid: No-show socks only in clearly casual contexts.

name: Case Diameter vs Wrist
mechanics: ~7" wrist → 38-40mm case; keep thickness under ~12mm to clear a cuff.

name: Strap Formality
mechanics: Steel > leather > rubber > NATO, most to least formal.
effect: Strap sets the watch's formality range.
use: Steel bracelet as the most versatile first choice.

name: Eyewear vs Face Shape
mechanics: Contrast, not echo — round face pairs with angular frames.
use: Your round Zweig frame is an echo — the second, angular frame fixes this.

name: Fragrance & Occasion
mechanics: EDT for office, EDP/parfum for evening. 1-2 sprays for office.
